plan.estimand: Mean group difference in participant-averaged responses
plan.hypothesis: Constant treatment effect of 0.45 on the group mean
assumptions: Random-intercept model with Gaussian responses
Marginal variance equals 1
Intraclass correlation is 0.4 across all participants
Treatment effect is constant across observations within and between participants
Groups equally allocated (1:1 ratio)
No missing data
Analysis via participant-level averaging followed by two-sided pooled t-test
Standard normality and homogeneity of variance assumptions for t-test apply
scientific_notes: The random-intercept structure implies: var(Y_ij) = τ² + σ² = marginal_var = 1, where τ² is between-participant variance and σ² is within-participant variance
Intraclass correlation ρ = τ²/(τ² + σ²) = 0.4, enabling decomposition of the marginal variance
Participant-level averaging reduces within-participant variability; the averaging variance is var(Ȳ_i) = τ² + σ²/m = 1 - 0.4(1 - 1/m) where m=4 is the number of observations per participant
Two-sided pooled t-test assumes equal variances across groups and uses the sampling distribution of (Ȳ_treatment - Ȳ_control) / SE
